initial_analysis.notes: Global deterministic transform likely inflates wavelet sigma and residual_intensity_corr; peel global first, then re-check noise on peeled residual per layer-peeling protocol.

noise_6step_check.diagnosis: YCrCb gaussian. Section-B IMPULSE/SPECKLE auto-verdicts are known false positives here: extreme_pct=68.6% and vm_slope=2.84 are inflated by residual deterministic mismatch + heavy clipping (clipped_fraction 0.486), not by impulse/speckle noise. Reliable evidence: (a) noise_prior channel sigma ratio 1.8 > 1.4 -> YCrCb (SKILL 10/10 rule); (b) isolated noise_gaussian_YCrCb:2 gave verify_signals noise:sigma + noise:clean_residual MATCH vs target; (c) rgb_ratio=1.477 > 1.4 post-peel. Severity: isolated sigma sev1=9.6 / sev2=14.2; with saturation applied after noise the estimate is amplified (nY2+satY3 -> 26.1), target 14.7 -> sev1 (nY1+satY4 -> 12.2) preferred over sev2.

final_decision.rationale: Signal mode (sigma=14.7 >= 2, PSNR unusable). Deterministic steps ruled out: no compression (block_boundary 1.003, unique_G 256), no blur (spectral_slope_ratio 0.993, FFT anisotropy 0, PCA 0.0). Global: HSV saturation darkens luma far too much (sat1 mean -31.2 vs target -16.8) and cannot reach chroma ratio 3.0 without mean collapse; YCrCb saturation leaves luma mean near-intact and explains chroma boost. Severity curve (alone, mean/var/chroma/clip): sev2 (-9.6/1.479/2.06/0.328), sev3 (-13.5/1.614/2.29/0.464), sev4 (-15.7/1.676/2.40/0.517), sev5 (-17.9/1.713/2.51/0.550). Final nYCrCb1+satYCrCb4: mean -15.3, var 1.629, chroma 3.156, clip 0.535, sigma 12.2 vs target -16.8/1.579/2.996/0.486/14.7 (all within ~10-17%, balanced optimum; satY5 fixes mean -17.5 but overshoots var 1.702 / clip 0.576 / chroma 3.474 and sigma 9.5). Noise type YCrCb per channel-sigma-ratio 1.8 and MATCHing noise signals. Cross-pair (pairs 1-4): noise:clean_residual matched all 4; pair4 PARTIAL (mean matched, var 16%); pairs 1-3 WEAK, attributable to content-dependent metrics on far more chromatic scenes (pair2 clownfish, pair1 supertrees) - SKILL warns cross-content metrics are unreliable. Alternatives kept: satYCrCb5 variant and noise_RGB2+satYCrCb3.

cross_pair_verification.note: Visual check of simulated vs degraded for pairs 1-3 shows matching saturated+noisy appearance; numeric cross-pair scatter reflects content dependence, not a different pipeline.

final_decision.reason: Candidate B improved signal-level agreement on 4/5 pairs (sigma 4/5 vs 2/5; variance 3/5 vs 2/5; mean diffs halved on pairs 2/3; aggregate 11/20 vs 8/20) but only pair0 transitioned WEAK->PARTIAL and pair4 regressed PARTIAL->WEAK. The instruction requires a majority of pairs WEAK->PARTIAL/MATCH for a noise-containing candidate to CHANGE; 1/5 is not a majority. The residual mean_shift mismatch (target -2..-3 on vivid pairs vs sim -9..-18 under every integer saturation severity) is structural to the YCrCb-saturation model and cannot be fixed by severity tuning. Per protocol: NO_CHANGE, R0 pipeline retained; candidate B recorded as alternative for downstream training-PSNR arbitration.
